boundaries.description: Harness-neutral front-end. Reads manifests, schema, anchor map, and profiles; produces the System2Graph IR. Contains no Claude rendering, hook-wiring, frontmatter-emission, or lock-formatting logic (REQ-040). Knows nothing about any backend.
The System2Graph schema (dataclasses). Pure data; depends only on ir/ sibling type modules (anchors, capabilities) and stdlib.
Assembles the graph from validated inputs. May import all neutral ir/ helpers. May not import any backend.
Manifest read/validation, schema + anchor-map loaders, injection scan. May import the vendored hook-security shim. Treats all input as untrusted; no dynamic execution.
The Backend lowering protocol. Imports only the IR graph type and stdlib typing.

The Claude projection. Consumes only the System2Graph and the project path. MUST NOT read overlay manifests, the anchor map, profiles, or the schema directly (REQ-015) — all needed data arrives via the IR. Owns all Claude byte-level details and the IR-anchor -> CLAUDE.md location mapping. Phase 4: its _build_degradation_report becomes a thin BYTE-PRESERVING wrapper over backends/_degradation.py (PG6); emitted bytes unchanged.

Internal, stdlib-only deterministic block-YAML serializer (emit-only; no parser). Pure helper for a closed block-YAML subset. Imports only stdlib. No knowledge of the IR, no I/O. No runtime consumer (retained as reworded shared infrastructure with direct unit coverage in evals/test_yaml_serializer.py).

Phase 4 (PG6): the shared, descriptor-driven degradation helper. Internal, stdlib-only, no I/O; backend-agnostic record assembly + the status->flags rule. Imports only stdlib (it receives ir.capabilities-as-data + a parsed descriptor dict as arguments — it does NOT import ir/*). Consumed by claude_code/pi only. BYTE-PRESERVING: each backend keeps its own envelope + 'fields' selection so the claude-code lock degradation_report bytes are unchanged.

Phase 4: the Pi backend (second backend; first MIXED-status backend). Consumes only the System2Graph + project path; same boundary as claude_code. Reads its own backends/capabilities/pi.json data file (a JSON read, not an ir/* import). Uses the shared backends/_degradation.py for the mixed degradation report. Emits the Pi extension TypeScript + Pi context/skill/prompt markdown + JSON lock as TEXT (no node/TS/third-party in the compiler; node/pi only in TESTS). MUST NOT read overlay manifests, the anchor map, profiles, or the schema (REQ-015). MUST NOT consume ir.base_template or ir.overlay_inputs (Claude-targeted; Pi renders from structured IR fields only). Owns DEFAULT dangerous-command + sensitive-path pattern sets (keeps the IR neutral). Output is a pure function of the IR (no timestamps).
Declarative per-backend capability descriptors (JSON: claude_code.json, pi.json). No code; loaded by the owning backend only. pi.json is the first MIXED descriptor (native + adapted + advisory).

Thin orchestration: parse args -> ir.compose -> select backend -> backend.{emit|uninstall|doctor|recompose_from_lock} -> render neutral warnings/reports. May import the front-end entry and the backend registry. Phase 4 registers 'pi'. Phase 5 (parity): a subcommand dispatcher (compile|uninstall|doctor|from-lock|profile) reaching FULL composer.py parity. Lifecycle verbs go through the GROWN Backend contract (the CLI stays target-agnostic; per-target lock parsing lives in the backend). Profiles are harness-NEUTRAL — the CLI MAY import ir/profiles.py for the profile verb (the one ir/ helper the CLI uses, since profiles feed compose for ANY target and are not a backend concern). Does not touch the plugin's /system2:* surface (additive).

Phase 5: build/CI tooling (NOT product modules). build_bundle.py generates the vendored plugin bundle by copying ir/+backends/+plugin_adapter verbatim and writing BUNDLE.json (the compiler-source hash). check_bundle_fresh.py is the CI staleness guard (regenerate -> hash -> compare -> fail-if-stale). May import stdlib only; reads compiler product source as files (a copy, not an import).

Phase 5 [PLUGIN]: the vendored, stdlib-only bundle the plugin ships — a VERBATIM COPY of the compiler's ir/ + backends/ (+ plugin_adapter.py + BUNDLE.json), generated by tools/build_bundle.py. Same internal boundaries as the compiler source (it IS the source). plugin_adapter.py preserves the composer.py flag CLI contract (maps --doctor/--uninstall/--from-lock/--profile/--save-profile/--profile-op/--profile-* onto ClaudeCodeBackend lifecycle + ir.compose + ir/profiles.py). Stdlib-only by construction; never adds a plugin runtime dependency (G7/C3).

Compiler's own golden suite. Invokes the frozen oracle as a subprocess (never imports it). From Phase 1, invokes the compiler in-process via ir.compose + backend.emit. Phase 4: also drives the pi backend, snapshots its artifacts as goldens, loads the generated .pi/extensions/system2.ts via node/pi and fires synthetic tool_call events for the PROVEN-BLOCKING test (LOUD SKIP when node/pi absent; never a silent pass), and drives the backend-parameterized mixed-status degradation fixture. Tests use a hermetic temp HOME and a hermetic .pi; they never touch the user's real ~/.pi or Pi config. May import backends/_degradation.py to drive the PG6 fixture. Stdlib-only harness.

global_invariants: No module under ir/ or backends/ imports any third-party package (stdlib only; REQ-016/043).
No module introduces network calls or telemetry (REQ-047).
backends/* receive all data via the System2Graph argument; a static test fails if any backend references manifest/anchor-map/profile/schema source files (REQ-015).
ir/* contains no Claude prompt-rendering, hook-wiring, or frontmatter-emission code (REQ-040).
The frozen plugin composer.py is never imported by product code; only the evals/ oracle runner touches it, and only via subprocess (REQ-006/017).

Phase 4 (PG6): the degradation report is built by the shared backends/_degradation.py for ALL backends; the refactor is BYTE-PRESERVING — the claude-code lock degradation_report is byte-identical to its pre-refactor golden (AC-P1), gated before any Pi code merges.

Phase 4: backends/_degradation.py imports only stdlib and never imports ir/* (it receives ir.capabilities-as-data + a parsed descriptor dict as arguments); the status->flags rule (native=>enforced:true,gated:false; adapted=>enforced:false,gated:true; advisory/unsupported=>both false) lives there as the single source of truth.

Phase 4: the ir/ schema and backends/claude_code.py are byte-unchanged by the Pi work (only its _build_degradation_report wrapper is rewired to the shared helper, preserving bytes); the Pi backend adds files under backends/ only (NFR-001) and consumes the shared System2Graph read-only.
Phase 4: ir.base_template and ir.overlay_inputs are Claude-targeted; backends/pi.py MUST NOT read them (renders from structured IR fields only).

Phase 4: PiBackend.emit is a pure function of the IR — no timestamps in emitted artifacts, no writes outside project_path; it never touches $HOME or the user's real ~/.pi. The compiler emits TS/markdown/JSON as TEXT; no node/TS/third-party import in the compiler (node/pi only in the evals/ tests).

Phase 4: the pi backend is the first MIXED-status backend — enforce-lease/block-dangerous/protect-sensitive are 'native' (generated extension on('tool_call') hard-block; Pi has no built-in permission system), budget is 'adapted', format/typecheck are 'advisory'; every IR capability appears in pi.json and in system2.pi.lock.json with a matching status (no silent drop, NFR-003/NFR-004).

Phase 4: dangerous-command + sensitive-path pattern sets are BACKEND-OWNED defaults in backends/pi.py (not in the IR), keeping the IR neutral; enforce-lease uses role write_scope when present, else is wired-but-unscoped and reported honestly (never a silent vacuous native claim).

Phase 5: the Backend contract GROWS to a per-target lifecycle (emit + uninstall + doctor + recompose_from_lock + lock helpers); Pi reaches feature-completeness, not just Claude. The boundary is unchanged — each backend imports only ir.graph (+ its helpers) + stdlib; the from-lock recompose path arrives as an IR; no backend reads manifests/anchor-map/profiles/schema directly.

Phase 5: profiles stay HARNESS-NEUTRAL and SHARED — the single ir/profiles.py feeds compose for ANY --target; the CLI's profile verb is the only place the CLI imports ir/profiles.py; there is no per-target profile surface.

Phase 5: the claude-code lifecycle (uninstall/doctor/from-lock) is a byte-faithful PORT of composer._uninstall/_uninstall_last_overlay/drift_check/from-lock (relocation, not rewrite); the CLI-contract goldens diff the compiler CLI (and the vendored bundle/shim) against the FROZEN pre-flip oracle's args/exit-codes/stdout/stderr (no auto-rebaseline; REQ-007 extends to the lifecycle verbs).

Phase 5: no Claude artifact bytes change (REQ-014 holds). The ONLY intentional non-Claude byte change is the additive overlay_sources[] key appended LAST to the pi lock (re-baselines that golden once, reviewed; asserted additive/last).

Phase 5 (convergence): the plugin ships a vendored, stdlib-only SUBTREE (plugin/scripts/_system2_compiler/) that is a VERBATIM copy of the compiler's product source -> byte-identical Claude output by construction; the plugin stays ZERO-DEPENDENCY (no pip/submodule/network; verified by a dep scan over the vendored subtree).

Phase 5 [PLUGIN] the flip is a THIN SHIM (not full-replace): composer.py/profiles.py become ~10-line shims delegating to the bundle via plugin_adapter, preserving the EXACT ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/composer.py flag CLI + exit codes + stdout/stderr the skills invoke -> the skills (compose/doctor/profile/init/uninstall) are UNCHANGED; the pre-flip composer.py is preserved as composer.py.preflip (immutable oracle baseline + one-commit reversible backout).

Phase 5 (G8/NFR-006): vendored-bundle freshness is MACHINE-ENFORCED — tools/check_bundle_fresh.py FAILS CI on a stale/hand-edited bundle (a stale bundle cannot merge) and system2:doctor surfaces bundle_freshness/bundle_tampered; a drift-guard self-test (mutate a vendored byte -> CI fails AND doctor reports tampered) proves the guard has teeth.

Phase 5 GATE: the flip is not merged until the bundle-equivalence gate (bundle output == compiler == frozen oracle, compose) is empty-diff, the CLI-contract goldens (all lifecycle verbs) are empty-diff, AND the plugin's own System2/evals/ suite is green on the flipped plugin.
